sections.name: File setup, base, calls
sections.title: Test setup and sample call builder
sections.what: Imports the test tools and the alterEgo engine. Defines one typical call record and a helper that makes a list of calls by copying that record and changing some fields.
sections.why: Lets each test describe only the fields that matter to it, which keeps the tests short and readable.
sections.watch_out: The sample calls are invented. Changing the base record changes every test in the file at once.

sections.name: Alter Ego identity model (alter-ego) (part 1)
sections.title: Reveal threshold, axes and modifiers
sections.what: Checks that nothing is revealed until ten graded calls exist. Checks that identical histories give identical output, that each of the five axes (risk, timing, calibration, contrarianism, domain mix) stays between 0 and 1 with a plain explanation, and that contrarianism stays empty when no crowd data exists. Also checks that the modifiers Steady, Sharp, Balanced and Contrarian are chosen under the right conditions.
sections.why: Likely reason: identity should come from enough evidence and should never be guessed. The threshold and the empty-data rule enforce that.
sections.watch_out: Explanation text is compared word for word, so a copy edit to an explanation will fail this test.

sections.name: Alter Ego identity model (alter-ego) (part 2)
sections.title: Persona mapping and no-evidence fallback
sections.what: Checks that each calling style maps to one persona: risk to The Professor, death-over timing to The Opener, tempo to The Architect, calibration to The Iceman, clutch to The Closer. Checks that timing is not judged on too few calls, that a file with no standout trait opens with the sport's analyst, and that a coin-flip caller is not named The Iceman.
sections.why: Likely reason: prevents a persona from being named on one lucky call or on no real pattern.
sections.watch_out: The timing rule needs at least three calls in each phase. Changing that minimum changes results for borderline histories without any visible error.

summary: Checks that the Alter Ego feature names a fan's persona only after enough graded calls, and that the same call history always gives the same result.
purpose: Protects the rules that turn a fan's past calls into a named persona such as The Opener or The Iceman, with a modifier such as Steady or Bold.
why: Likely reason: the feature must reveal a persona only when there is real evidence, so the tests pin the thresholds and fallbacks.
how: Builds synthetic call histories by copying one base call and changing a few fields. Runs alterEgo on each history and checks the reveal threshold, determinism, the five axis values and their explanations, the persona mapping, the modifiers, and the no-evidence fallback.
inputs: Synthetic IdentityCall records created inside the test file. No real user data.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the vitest runner.
risks: The tests fix exact explanation sentences and exact thresholds. Any change to wording or to a threshold will fail tests even when the behaviour is acceptable.
debug: Run only this file. Read the first failing expect line, then compare the persona, modifier and axis values it reports with the thresholds in the alterEgo engine module.
